Definition: sight, whether abstractly (vision) or concretely (a spectacle)
BiblicalUsage: When the text says rŏʼîy, it means sight, whether abstractly (vision) or concretely (a spectacle). In 1 Samuel 16:12, we read, "…Now he ruddy, withal of a beautiful countenance…"; in Genesis 16:13, "…I also here looked after him that seeth…". You hear it again in Job 7:8 — "The eye of him that hath seen me…" — and in Nahum 3:6, "And I will cast abominable filth upon thee…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe rŏʼîy matters because God chose this word, and it tells the truth about how God deals with his people. I believe rŏʼîy is still true for us, because the God who gave it has not changed his mind.
